# Gross domestic product, other aggregates of national accounts and employment, 2025

## 1.5% economic growth in 2025

After revision of annual estimates, Slovenia’s gross domestic product for 2025 was estimated at EUR 71,171 million. Compared to the previous year, it grew by 5.5% in nominal terms and by 1.5% in volume terms. The data for the three preceding years were routinely revised.

Moderate economic growth
Slovenia’s gross domestic product for 2025 was estimated at EUR 71,171 million based on annual data sources. This was a 5.5% nominal increase over the previous year, whereas in volume terms the 2025 GDP grew by 1.5%. Economic growth continued to slow down in 2025 after it was 2.6% in 2023 and 2.0% in 2024.
GDP volume growth based on annual data sources is 0.5 of a percentage point higher than the quarterly estimate published on 16 February 2026.
Output increased in real terms by 1.0% and intermediate consumption by 0.5%.
The largest contributions to GDP growth in 2025 came from information and communication activities, financial and insurance activities, and construction; each of these three sections contributed 0.3 of a percentage point.

## Taiwan-Portugal Economic Relations

2026-01-13

Trade

Bilateral trade between Taiwan and Portugal reached US$ 761 million in 2025, ranking Portugal our 18th largest trading partner in Europe. In 2025, Taiwan's exports to Portugal were US$ 564 million, representing a decrease of 8.69% over the previous year, making Portugal our 14th largest export market in Europe. Meanwhile, Taiwan's imports from Portugal decreased 5.74% to US$ 197 million, and ranking Portugal our 20th largest source of imports in Europe.

 

Investment

As of 2025, Portuguese enterprises have invested a total of 64 cases in Taiwan, with a cumulative value of US$ 241 million. Major investment industries were: accommodation and food services, electronic components manufacturing, wholesale and retail Trade and arts, entertainment, and recreation services. ## Poslovne priložnosti za slovenska podjetja na Tajvanu

Torek, 8. julij 2025, ob 10.00

Spoštovani,

v sodelovanju z Taiwan Trade Center Budapest vas vabimo, da se udeležite spletnega seminarja z naslovom Poslovne priložnosti za slovenska podjetja na Tajvanu, ki bo potekal v torek, 8. julija 2025, ob 10. uri. Na dogodku bo priložnosti za sodelovanje s Tajvanom predstavil g. Mark Liu, direktor Taiwan Trade Center Budapest. Delovni jezik dogodka bo angleščina.

Ste že razmišljali o vstopu na enega najbolj tehnološko naprednih azijskih trgov?

Tajvan velja za eno najpomembnejših azijskih gospodarstev in strateškega partnerja EU, še posebej na področjih naprednih tehnologij, polprevodnikov, zelene transformacije, elektronskih komponent in medicinske opreme. Gre za izredno inovativno, stabilno in izvozu usmerjeno okolje. V zadnjih letih je Tajvan beležil nadpovprečno gospodarsko rast, ki jo poganja visokotehnološka industrija, digitalna preobrazba ter odprtost za sodelovanje z evropskimi podjetji. Med ključne podatke velja izpostaviti, da Tajvan ustvari več kot 40 % svetovne proizvodnje polprevodnikov ter se uvršča med deset najbolj konkurenčnih gospodarstev na svetu.

Udeležba na dogodku je brezplačna, prijava pa obvezna do 4. julija 2025. V primeru odpovedi po tem datumu ali neudeležbe brez predhodne odjave se zaračuna no-show fee v višini 50 EUR. Povezava do prijave bo posredovana prijavljenim udeležencem dan pred dogodkom.

# The Hungarian Trade Office in Taipei Visited with CIECA Chairman Joseph Lyu

2025/02/17

Show Details

On 17th February, Mr. Gergely Kádár, Representative of the Hungarian Trade Office in Taipei, and Mr. Balázs Szabó, Investment and Trade Director visited CIECA and was received by Chairman Joseph Lyu. During the meeting, they exchanged views on bilateral economic and trade relations between Taiwan and Hungary, also touched upon global economic trends and the development of specific industries of finance, investment, and agriculture. Representative Kádár noted that Taiwan-Hungary economic and trade exchanges had reached a significant scale, with major Taiwanese companies such as Giant, Sinbon, and Foxconn having made substantial investments in Hungary. “In addition to automotive, biotechnological, and pharmaceutical industries, Hungary has also made progress in the FinTech sector; the Hungarian FinTech Association is planning a visit to Taiwan in November this year,” Director Szabó added. Chairman Lyu shared his professional insights on finance and expressed his hope for the continued development of bilateral economic and trade cooperation between Taiwan and Hungary.

## TaiwanICDF and ESTDEV Sign MoU Advancing Democratic Resilience, Digital Transformation, and Global Development Cooperation

2026-06-09

With the facilitation of the Taipei Mission in the Republic of Latvia, the International Cooperation and Development Fund (TaiwanICDF) has established a partnership with the Estonian Centre for International Development (ESTDEV), Estonia’s dedicated agency for official development assistance. The two sides formally signed a medium- to long-term Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) on June 8, 2026, marking a new milestone toward a more institutionalized and enduring partnership in international development cooperation between Taiwan and Estonia.
The MoU was signed at the Estonia Parliament (Riigikogu) by Secretary General Dr. Yu-Lin Huang of TaiwanICDF and Director General Andrea Kivi of ESTDEV, witnessed by Amb. Winston Wen-Yi Chen of the Taipei Mission in Latvia and Chairman Kristo Enn Vaga of Estonia-Taiwan Support Group of the Riigikogu. Centered on international development assistance, the partnership will focus on key areas including democratic governance, digital and social development, capacity building, and international engagement, reflecting a shared commitment by democratic partners to promote global sustainable development and strengthen societal resilience.
Estonia is widely recognized as a global leader in digital governance, with extensive experience in e-government, digital public services, and cybersecurity governance. Taiwan, on the other hand, has built strong expertise in democratic governance, digital innovation, and international development cooperation. Building on these complementary strengths, the two sides will advance collaboration along four strategic directions:
First, strengthening democratic governance and public sector capacity to enhance policy planning and governance effectiveness in partner countries;
Second, promoting digital transformation and technological innovation to support inclusive and sustainable development models;
Third, exploring joint cooperation opportunities in Eastern Europe, Africa, and other partner countries to leverage synergies and complementary resources;
Fourth, establishing mechanisms for knowledge sharing and policy dialogue to deepen professional exchange and talent development.
TaiwanICDF noted that this partnership with ESTDEV not only underscores the strong alignment between Taiwan and like-minded countries on democratic values and international development priorities, but also further expands Taiwan’s global development cooperation network. Through jointly designed and implemented development initiatives, both sides aim to enhance partner countries’ resilience in addressing digital transformation, governance challenges, and global risks, while contributing concrete outcomes toward the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
The signing of this MoU injects new momentum into Taiwan–Estonia relations and demonstrates both sides’ commitment to advancing international development cooperation grounded in shared democratic values. Looking ahead, TaiwanICDF and ESTDEV will continue to deepen substantive exchanges and collaboration, working together to build a more resilient and inclusive global development cooperation network.
